questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Be ready to change your lane position as conditions change, especially when riding at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see your motorcycle as easily as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should NOT:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake suddenly.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's stopping power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's stopping power.
Should only be used when the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's stopping power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow the group down as the leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them easily.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should change based on riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: Your cushion of space should increase when your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead clearly, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line works best for normal riding. However, switch to a single-file line when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which protects a motorcyclist best?

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: Where do motorcycles and other vehicles most often have conflicts?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Always use extra caution when approaching and riding through intersections.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: In the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
In the right side of the lane.
In either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: What is a motorcycle horn useful for?

options.text: It can quickly get someone's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help get someone's attention fast. However, motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns, so other drivers may not hear you. Never rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help you avoid serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble—it will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road quickly. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: How do you stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes together.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where should you ride if hazards are on your left?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses do not provide enough protection. In Vermont, you do not have to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To reduce your chance of a crash, make yourself visible. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT required for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: Good eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, give you a clear side view, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. They must also fit with eyeglasses or sunglasses underneath.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Focus only on moving through the intersection.
Speed up so others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still do not see them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that reduces your space cushion and helps you be seen.
One that increases your space cushion and helps you be seen.
One that increases road hazards and lets others pass you.
One that reduces road hazards and lets you follow vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that increases your space cushion and helps you be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed. Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion.
